slowest_experiments.experiment: V612 independent evidence capstone and V613 handoff
Independent contrast balance and leakage audit

summary: Eight experiments completed in 11.5 minutes. The sole compute-bound experiment, Three-family contrast feature bank, took 10.01 minutes and set the critical path; GPU idle on compute-bound work was false, but the single-process monitor finding makes inference batching the clearest throughput opportunity.
bottlenecks_identified: Three-family contrast feature bank was the 10.01-minute compute critical path within the 11.5-minute milestone window; the supplied data does not provide a finer phase-level cause.
The GPU monitor detected a single Python inference process and recommended batching more questions per forward pass, indicating an inference-batching bottleneck rather than GPU idleness.
Disk-mtime reconstruction supplies experiment-level duration but not task-scoped phase, batch-size, model-count, or runner-selection evidence.
improvements_suggested: Batch 8-16 questions per forward pass in the single Python inference process.
Record task-scoped phase timings and batch-size receipts for compute-bound inference.
Record model count and runner selection at launch so DualGPURunner applicability is auditable without enforcing it for single-model work.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add 8-16-question batching to the inference path.
Emit task-owned phase, batch-size, and GPU-utilization receipts for compute-bound work.
Emit launch-time model-count and runner-selection receipts.
meta_reflection: The 65% milestone-wide estimate applies the monitor's 4x lower-bound throughput gain only to the 10.01-minute compute task and leaves the rest of the 11.5-minute window unchanged. The data confirms accelerator engagement but does not establish that any task loaded 2 or more models in parallel, so no missed DualGPURunner dispatch is claimed.
